newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Zapatistas to return to peace talks -reports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Zapatistas to return to peace talks -reports.

text.p: Mexico's Zapatista rebels have agreed in general terms to resume peace talks with the government, Mexico City newspapers reported on Sunday.
The Zapatista rebels (EZLN), whose stronghold is in the southern state of Chiapas, broke off peace talks in early September after accusing the government of acting in bad faith.

"The EZLN has told us that it is in agreement with our proposals, although there are still some particular points outstanding," the newspaper Reforma quoted Jose Narro Cespedes, the president of the govenment negotiating committee (Cocopa), as saying.
"The important thing is that they have accepted in general terms to the proposals made by the Cocopa," he said.
The Zapatistas have been confined to their jungle strongholds in Chiapas since their January 1994 uprising.
